(= Pali vipāceti), grumbles, makes disapproving remarks: ˚yanti (= Tib. kha zer ba, acc. to = mukhara, loquacious, but Lex. also abusive);;;; ˚yati, but here vipācayati (= Pali), and Tib. rnam par smod pa, speaks abusively; always the third of a series of near-synonyms, avadhyāyati (Skt.) and kṣipati (Skt.; in dhriyati, in perhaps kṣīyati, q.v., in a similar context) being the others; in Pali, ujjhāyati khīyati vipāceti. (= AMg. visohaya; Skt. viśodhayati plus aka), purifying, one who purifies: ˚kāni … kalyāṇamitrāṇy āvaraṇīyānām; (uttarottara-)˚ko 'yaṃ … mārgo; in su-vi˚ and dur-vi˚, adj. Bhvr., like Pali dubbisodha (s.v. visodha), easy (hard) to purify; in view of su-vijñāpaka (q.v.), used in the same context, the lit. mg. seems to be well (ill) taking (i.e. subject to, controllable by) a purifier (were it not for the clear mg. of vijñāpaka, n. ag., we might interpret -viśodha plus -ka, having good, or bad, purification): (kaccid bhagavan sattvāḥ svākārāḥ suvijñāpakāḥ) suvineyāḥ suviśodhakā(ḥ)? mā haiva bhagavataḥ khedam utpādayanti ? (to a Buddha), I hope, Lord, your creatures are of good character (‘form’), easily instructed, … easily purified, and do not cause you trouble? the answer, line 10, repeats the epithets, ending (line 11) na ca me khedaṃ janayanti viśodhyamānāḥ, and cause me no trouble in being purified; note also the gdve. su-vineyāḥ, easily disciplined, in the context; it is impossible to understand -vijñāpaka and -viśodhaka here as karmadhārayas, well instructing and well purifying; in this way, therefore, we must also interpret: (sattvān … svākārān) suviśodhakān durākārān durviśodhakān; (katamaḥ sattvaḥ śuddhaḥ svākāraḥ) suvineyaḥ suvijñāpakaḥ suviśodhako … (repeated in essence 9 and); Tib. seems to support this, go sla ba (= su-vijñāp˚, facile à instruire,), sbyaṅ sla ba (facile à purifier).

, or ˚tī, corruptly ˚gatī in, a high number:, cited from (where all mss. and both edd. g for v) = Tib. rnam par brdaḥ śes ldan (ldan = possessing, -vant); so Tib. on; both edd. of ˚vatir (n. sg.); the true reading may have been ˚vatī; cf. s.v. saṃjñā (7).

(m.c. for Pali vissandati = Skt. viṣyandate), flows forth: pūrā mukhato visaṃdetsuḥ (so one ms., v.l. visaṃhetsu; em. viṣyandensu; first syllable short) (vs).

(m.?), (1) acc. to Tib. minor joint (of the body): (asmākaṃ …) saṃdhi-visaṃdhayaś ca duḥkhanti (prose), and our joints and minor joints (so Tib., tshigs daṅ tshigs phreḥu) ache; (2) in (vs) the same two words occur, and the mg. is not clear: (one who masters the) saṃdhiṃ visaṃdhiṃ ca vijānate 'sau (Tib. des ni mtshams daṅ tshigs [both mtshams and tshigs = saṃdhi] kyaṅ rab tu śes) sarveṣu dharmeṣu vilakṣaṇāni, prajānate artha niruktayaś ca yathā ca taṃ jānati bhāṣate tathā, perhaps he understands each connection and (minor?) interconnection, of various sorts (vilakṣaṇāni, prob. adj. with the two nouns) in all states of existence …

, adj. (= Pali id.; cf. sabhāga), different, unlike, discordant, inappropriate, uncongenial: te ca vilakṣaṇa te ˚gāḥ (vs); see s.v. udāra for id.; ˚ga-sattvānunayāt, thru attachment (see [Page503-b] anunaya) to people of the wrong sort (one may be dissuaded from the solitary life); (sarvasattvānāṃ) ˚ga-samavadhānabhayābhyanta-(read ˚ātyanta-)-vigamāya, in order to complete divorce for all creatures from the fear of association with uncongenial (people); ˚ga-sarvasamavadhānabhayabhītānāṃ ˚ga-sarvasamavadhānabhayavinivartanatāyai; a-visabhāga-varṇā, I (have come to be) of no discordant external appearance (foll. by avaivarta-varṇā, avikalpa-v˚, anīla-v˚, etc., long series of chiefly negative adj. ending in -varṇā); anyathā tu ˚gaṃ bhavati nirmāṇam ātmanaḥ, but otherwise (if it were not created in his own image) the magic creation (of a Bodhisattva) will be one inappropriate to himself; visabhāgāśaya (upāya), one of the six upāya (q.v.) of a Bodhisattva, viz. that (method) in which the mental disposition (of the Bodhisattva) is (represented as being) discordant (with its real nature, in order to influence and help creatures; he may make it appear that he is angry and hostile towards the recalcitrant, tho he never is), cf..

(unrecorded; v.l. vipādayati, Skt., reported only from, but since vipadyate is common in Skt. its caus. is likely to be the true reading here), brings to disaster, ruins: sa (sc. nāstikaḥ) ātmānam api (as well as others) ˚dayati.

(nonce-formation, pendant to saṃbhavati), becomes non-existent, passes away: (sarvadharmāḥ …) na saṃbhavanti na visaṃbhavanti. they do not come into being nor pass away (, strangely, influence each other).
, m., or nt., a high number, = Tib. ḥphro yas: ˚ram (cited from);;.

(= Pali vissajjeti), answers (a question), replies: ko nv atra samarthaḥ syād etam arthaṃ ˚jayituṃ, … to reply to this matter; etāṃ yo praśnāṃ ˚jeti tasya dhītā ca dīyati …, whoever answers these questions, to him is given my daughter; (anye praśnān) pṛcchanti anye ˚jayanti; (yadi … praśnān paripṛccheyur yān sa) … na śaknuyād ˚jayitum, … which he could not answer; (pṛṣṭā mayā pūrvakās tathāgatā …) taiś cāpi visarjitaṃ, similarly, and they replied; sa ca mayaivaṃ ˚jitas tūṣṇībhāvena prakrāntaḥ, and being thus answered by me, he departed in silence.
(= Pali vissajjetar; n. ag. to prec.), one who answers (questions): (praśnaprabhedakuśalaś ca bhavet praśnakoṭīnayutaśatasahasrāṇāṃ) ˚jayitā.

, in (prose) sa tābhyāṃ yāvat trir apy ukto visāriṇī kṛṣṇā nivāryamāṇā (so text, em., mss. ˚ṇau, intending ˚ṇo, which read) nāvatiṣṭhate, he (the king), tho spoken to (in admonition) by those two (ministers) as many as three times, being held back … did not remain (in good conduct; he kept backsliding into evil ways). The words visāriṇī kṛṣṇā perhaps corruptly represent an abl. phrase, from his evil course (cf. kṛṣṇa 1). As they stand, they could apparently only be a strange parenthetical clause; the corruption (? visāriṇī, or viśār˚ ?) was black (dark, evil). The Index to ed. renders kṛṣṇā by tongue of fire, which seems unacceptable; presumably it takes visā˚ as spreading; but even with the em. to nivāryamāṇā this hardly gives an intelligible result.
, adj. (= Pali vissaṭṭha), clear, distinct (of voice, speech): visṛṣṭaś ca (of Buddhaʼs voice, svara; in [Page504-a] a list of epithets); ˚ṭena svareṇa … svādhyāyaṃ karontī, of a female ascetic.
, m.,, or visoda, nt.,, = Tib. (b)rgyud yas, a high number; in cited from, which reads viśodha or viśrātas, corr. visrotas, qq.v.

, (1) nt. = Skt. m., (great) extent: mohapaṭala- ˚raṃ bhinnaṃ (n. sg.) (vs); (2) m. (special application of Skt.; Pali vitthāra similarly used), the full text (of a cliché, or well-known passage) is to be supplied, an indication of abbreviation: vistaraḥ (the full text meant is found in); usually instr. adv. vistareṇa, (supply) in full,; ˚ṇa kāryam, the text is to be done (i.e. recited) in full; the text may be specifically named, ˚reṇa rākṣasīsūtraṃ (chap. 8) sarvaṃ vādyam; vistareṇa yāvat, (read) in full (the part here omitted) as far as … (the foll. words resume the text at a later point);;;;; cf. peyāla, similarly used, and vistīrṇa; (3) (= Skt. Lex. id.; Skt. viṣṭara, M. viṭṭhara), seat: netrāṇi cābharaṇa-vāhana-vistarāṃś ca dattvā … (vs), (Buddhas) having given away their eyes, and ornaments, vehicles, and seats; (4) in (vs) gṛha-vistaraḥ should mean (or represent a word that means) a poor, mean house (see description): divyaṃ cāsya sudhābhaktam ayaṃ ca gṛha-vi˚, suviruddham iti kṛtvā jāto me hṛdi saṃśayaḥ (mss. ˚yam), heavenly is his nectar-food, and (yet) this is a miserable house … I suspect a corruption. But agrees. Perhaps, after all, and (merely) this is the size of the house (?).

, (1) (in Skt. only trans.; back-formation from caus. vistārayati ?; but simple star- recorded once as intrans., see), becomes widespread, appears everywhere: tadā vividhāni kalpavṛkṣā ˚ranti, cūtavṛkṣā (text cyūta˚) ˚ranti; (2) pass. vistīryate, is set forth at length, is explained: (nāvagacchāmi) ˚yatāṃ vacanam etad, I donʼt understand, explain this statement; cf. vistīraṇa.
, prob. read ˚rī-k˚ with, spreads far and wide, distributes: Bhagavad-dhātuṃ ca ˚kariṣyati.
(adj., = Pali vitthārika, extensive), ˚kaiḥ, adv., extensively: ˚kaiḥ puja (m.c. for pūjāṃ) karoti prasannacitto (vs); adj., -vistārikaṃ v.l. of most mss. for text -vaistārikaṃ; see vaistārika.
(nt.; to vistīryate, see s.v. vistarati 2, plus ana), full explanation: akalpāvikalpa-dharmanaya-˚ṇacakraṃ, the wheel that sets forth in detail the principles of the Doctrine …

, adj.-ppp., nt. ˚ṇam, (supply) in full, like vistaraḥ, ˚reṇa (see vistara 2) used to mark abbreviation of a fuller text: yadā dāni ekaṃ pārśvaṃ pakvaṃ bhavati, vistīrṇam, atha dvitīyena pārśvena. So I interpret the word; ʼs interpretation seems to me impossible; I admit, however, that I do not know the full text here abbreviated.
, n. of a former Buddha:. No v.l.; but Tib. ḥod, light, instead of ˚bheda (indicating rather ˚tejas, or ˚prabha, or the like).

, only bad writing for Skt. viṣṭhita, ppp. of vi plus sthā, s.v. 3, stood still: sarvā nadyaś ca ˚tāḥ (vs); so with ms. A; vv.ll. tiṣṭhatāḥ, tiṣṭhitāḥ; the latter could be a MIndic ppp. to pres. tiṣṭhati.]

(cf. AMg. viṇhāvaṇaka, a bath in holy water; no other form or deriv. of vi-snā-has been found outside of a etym.), bathes (trans.): visnapī (aor.) nāyakaṃ (vs); (paramasurabhigandhodaka-)kalaśair visnāpya (prose).

, nt. (= Pali vipphandita; orig. ppp. of Skt. vi-spand-), twitching; motion: ˚ta-mātra-parāyaṇaṃ mīnakulam avekṣya, perceiving the tribe of fish engaged in nothing more than twitching (in a nearly dry pond); (teṣāṃ sattvānāṃ citta-)carita- ˚tāni jñāsyati.
(vi plus Skt. spṛś-,), mishandles, maltreats: (ye 'pi mām ākrośeyur) visparśeyus tāḍayeyuḥ … (prose).
(Skt. only nt. ˚na), the causing astonishment:, see s.v. toṣaṇā.
, in, read (Skt.) vismāpana, (causing) astonishment; so Tib., ṅo mtshar; parasya ˚nahetu kurvati.]

, adj.-ppp., with karpāsa or kār˚, lit. broken, dissolved cotton, i.e. prob. cotton batting, cotton wool: vihataṃ kārpāsaṃ (v.l. kar˚) ubhayatrāśraye saṃstaritavyaṃ, tatra etāni aṇḍakāni … nikṣiptavyāni upari vihataṃ kārpāsaṃ (mss. kar˚) tam ete mātṛkārthaṃ poṣiṣyati (vihataṃ is read only in the second occurrence in one ms., but the other readings prob. intend it).

, quasi-MIndic ppp. or subst. (to Skt. vihanyate, is distressed), either distressed, or (subst.) distress: kiṃ ti (= te) ˚yitena (vs); if ti (te) is instr., lit., what use is there of you(r being) distressed?; if gen., what is the use of your distress?

, rarely ˚te (perh. m.c.), (= Pali id.) lives, dwells, spends oneʼs time, in very general sense: usually = Tib. gnas (pa), e.g.; sarve saddharmaguravo vyahārṣur (so read) viharanti ca, athāpi vihariṣyanti eṣa buddheṣu dharmatā, all (sc. Buddhas, past, present, and future) lived, live, and will live showing respect for the Good Law; this is the nature of Buddhas (= Pali, where the preceding prose makes the mg. clear; is unsatisfactory); Buddhavihāreṇa viharan, living in the way of life of a B., = Tib. saṅs rgyas kyi gnas pas gnas pa; something like this is prob. meant by, vihārakuśalo dhīro tatra (viz. in the city of Ratanakholaka) viharate muniḥ (vs), the wise Sage (Buddha) dwells there, knowing the right way (or the way appropriate to him, the Buddhaʼs way) to live (sees in vihāra-kuśalo a reference to the four brahma-vihāra, which I doubt; cf. s.v. vihāra 2); buddha-vihāreṇa vatādya Tathāgato viharati, jina-vi˚ sarvajñatā-vi˚ mahānāga-vihāreṇa vatādya Tathāgato viharati, atītānāgatapratyutpannān vā tathāgatān … samanusmarati, the Tathāgata is dwelling in the Buddha-state etc.; divyehi vihārehi āniñjehi vihārehi sāntatyehi vihārehi buddho buddha-vihārehi … (etc.) tehi tehi vihārehi viharati, … (Buddha) dwells in (various) states (conditions or modes of life); similarly; tadāpy ahaṃ bhagavan yadbhūyastvenānenaiva vihāreṇa viharāmi, even then, Lord, I mostly live in this same state (here, of mind); there follows a quotation of the speakerʼs thoughts; hence at least one Chin. translator renders I think, using the same character which elsewhere renders cintayati; Tib. seems to render mchi ba (come, go, appear): rtag par nam mchi ba deḥi tshe bcom Idan ḥdas ḥdi ltar; (p. xxiii) renders a similar phrase passe par les états dʼesprit in ekapiṇḍapātreṇāhaṃ ānanda traimāsaṃ niṣīdiṣyaṃ purimakānāṃ tathāgatānāṃ … vihārehi vihariṣyaṃ, … I will dwell in the states of being (mind?) of the former Buddhas, which he then does; (Mañjuśrīḥ …) imaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ saṃprakāśayamānaḥ sukhasparśaṃ (v.l. sukhasaṃsparśaṃ) viharati, … dwells in a happy condition.
(so also; app. to vi-han-),, [Page505-a] prob. the being subject to damage, spoliation, or frustration; Tib. rnam par ñams par byas pa, (to be) made much damaged; so essentially Chin.

, m. (Pali id.), in BHS chiefly in two mgs., both seemingly based on the meaning dwelling (to viharati, q.v.), (1) dwelling place of monks, esp. of a monkish community, monastery; so used also in Skt.: in this sense = Tib. gtsug lag khaṅ, house of sciences, because schools were associated with monasteries,;; (2) = Tib. gnas (pa), as for viharati, state of being, stage or condition of existence; sukhasparśa-vihāra-tā; brahma-vi˚, q.v.; see s.v. viharati for examples; others praviṣṭamānasya śubhair vihārair (vs), prob. being entered into (instr. = loc.) fair states; mayā pramattavihārāye na samanvāhṛtaṃ (so read with mss.), by me (a devatā), in a negligent state, it was not considered that …, proved by vs version of same incident, mamedaṃ na viditaṃ pramattāye; ayaṃ (sc. Maitreyaʼs dwelling, Vairocanavyūhālaṃkāragarbha) śūnyatānimittāpraṇihita-vihāra-vihāriṇām āvāsaḥ, and long list of similar formulae, all with cpds. ending -vihāravihāriṇāṃ, the abode of those who dwell in the state of …; yat Tathāgataḥ tribhir … apratisamair vihāraiḥ tadbahula-vihārī, āryeṇa vihāreṇa, divyena, brāhmeṇa; iyam asya vihāraparamatety ucyate. tatra śūnyatānimittāpraṇihita-vihārā (cf. above) nirodhasamāpattivihārāś cāryavihāra ity ucyate; catvāri dhyānāny ārupyasamāpattayaś ca divyo vihāra ity uc˚; catvāry apramāṇāni (= brahmavihāra) brāhmo vi˚ …; twelve bodhisattva-vihāra, listed and explained at length in the ‘vihāra-chapter (paṭala)’ of, (there is a 13th, the tāthāgato vi˚, niruttaro vi˚,), listed, gotra-vi˚, adhimukticaryā-vi˚, pramudita-vi˚, adhiśīla-vi˚, etc. (the long chapter must be read to understand the terms which by themselves sound obscure); ten jñānapāramitāvihāra, (listed); in the standard 10 bodhisattva-bhūmi (q.v.) are called b˚-vihārāḥ (line 23); cf. comm., ekādaśa vihārā ekādaśa bhūmayaḥ (the 11th is the buddha-bhūmi); (3) prob. walking (as in Skt.), in two almost identical passages in : padā vihāra and, also in (printed as cpd.), and, walking, marching on foot (refers to passing around a holy place to the right,); below, mālāvihāraḥ kṛtaḥ and, and, a garland-perambulation (?), precise mg. not clear to me; it is obviously some form of homage to the holy spot, more elaborate than the depositing of loose flowers (muktapuṣpāṇi;).

, dwelling, living (not markedly different from some Skt. uses but with the flavor of BHS vihāra, viharati): -vimokṣa-vihārī; sarvadharmasamatā-˚rī; others;, and s.v. vihāra (2), e.g.;; pratyakṣa-˚riṇo hy ete bodhisattvā atra sthāne, existing in visible presence.
, may be MIndic for Skt. vidhu, moon, as in Pkt. (), or, perh. more likely, for Skt. vibhu, lord, in mokṣa-vihūnām (sc. bodhisattvānām) (vs), lords (or moons) of salvation.
, adj. (subst.; = Pali id.; to viheṭhayati plus -aka), one who injures; injurious, doing harm, troubling: (of Māra);;;;;;;; neg. a-vi˚.
, nt., and ˚nā (= Pali ˚na; to viheṭhayati), injury, hurting, doing harm, violating: ājñā-˚nam; (a-)˚na- (in cpd.); ˚nā;;;; (so read with ms.);; ˚nābhiprāya (with ˚na or ˚nā?).

(m.; Pali id.; Skt. see below), falcon: sa hatas tv itaraṃ hanti ˚seneva pakṣiṇaḥ, he however, himself destroyed, destroys others, as birds (are killed) by a falcon; so, acc. to, Tib. (= Pali ˚soka), n. of a brother of Aśoka:; Vītaśokāvadāna =, colophon (story of how he was converted to Buddhism after originally being an adherent of heretics).

(also spelled ˚seti, ˚sati, ˚śati; for *vy-atikāśayati), lets light shine through; with synonym vītiloketi, in: gopānasī(ye)-antarāṇi (and, pāṃśulikāntarāṇi) … [Page506-a] vītilokenti vītikāśenti (vītiloketsuḥ vītikāśetsuḥ, with minor variants);;;; in the parallel virājante, vyavabhāsante.

(to vyākaroti; in mg. 1 essentially like Skt. id.; Pali id. also in mg. 3), (1) explanation, elucidation, esp. of questions put: praśnasya ˚ṇena; dharmaṃ paripṛcchakās, tasya ca ˚ṇena tuṣṭā(ḥ) …; sarvapraśna-˚ṇa-; (rājā …) pṛcchati, te ca jñātvā vyākaronti, teṣāṃ vyākaraṇaṃ śrutvā …; ˚ṇe bhāṣyamāṇe; prob. in this sense, persons like the Bodhisattva are called ˚ṇa-saṃpannāḥ, perfect in elucidation (of religious problems), (in one of the reproaches hurled at Māra; cf. pratibhānasaṃpannāḥ 18, just before); so also the Pratyekabuddhas who entered nirvāṇa to ‘empty’ the earth for the birth of Śākyamuni are said to have vyākaraṇāni vyākaritvā, before entering nirvāṇa; in this case the vyākaraṇāni are the khaḍgaviṣāṇa gāthās appropriate to Pratyekabuddhas; there are four technical kinds of ˚ṇa, [Page517-a] answers to questions, in, ekāṃśa-, vibhajya-, paripṛcchā-, and sthāpanīya-˚ṇa, qq.v.; as one of the 12 or 9 types of literature in the canon, ˚ṇam;, explanation, perh. more specifically answers to questions, = vaiyākaraṇa, Pali veyyākaraṇa (which acc. to means all the Abhidhamma, suttas without gāthās, and whatever else is not included in the other 8 divisions!); not predictions with and; (2) vyākaraṇaḥ, m., (see), if correct would be nom. ag., expounder, elucidator; parallels; vaiyākaraṇaḥ, in Skt. and perh. here grammarian; (3) (as in Pali, not Skt.) prophecy, prediction, recorded only of a prediction that someone will attain perfect enlightenment (tho the verb vyākaroti is not so restricted); in this sense very common, regularly with gen. of the person (or in comp.) and loc. of the goal: Śāriputrasyedaṃ ˚ṇam anuttarāyāṃ samyaksambodhau; similarly;;, etc. etc.; megha-māṇavaka-˚ṇaṃ; ˚ṇaṃ … labheyā, may I get a prophecy; apramāṇa-˚ṇa-pratyeṣakaś; others, etc., common everywhere; exceptionally, with loc. of beneficiary, gen. of maker of the prophecy, vyākaraṇam asmi (mss. asmiṃ) dyutimatŏ, so read, the Glorious Oneʼs prophecy about him.

(and other, MIndic presents; also viyā˚; in mg. 1 not only = Pali but also Skt., see s.v. 2, hence only a few exx. here; cf. vyākaraṇa), (1) elucidates, esp. a question: … paripṛccheyaṃ, yathā me bhagavāṃ vyākariṣyati …; (see vyākaraṇa 1); bhagavān taṃ arthaṃ vyākare; vyākuruṣva … kuta eti (with Ḱ enti) ime śūrā (vs); asminn arthe vyākriyamāṇe and; ity eṣā pañcamī bhūmī (mss. ˚myāṃ!) vyākṛtā … (vs); nāpi ye dharmāḥ vyākṛtās te avyākṛtā iti deśayāmi; (2) (= Pali id.) prophesies, predicts, in general: (naimittikair vaipañcikaiś ca) vyākṛtam abhūt: maṅgaladvāreṇa kumāro 'bhiniṣkramiṣyatīti; similarly;; so (sc. naimittikaḥ) 'pi tathaivāmṛtādhigamanam eva vyākṛtavān; (naimittikehi kumāro) vyākṛtaḥ, rājā cakravartī bhaviṣyati; (naimittikena ca) horapāṭhakena ca vyākṛto, yena kāryeṇa devadatto kumāro abhiniṣkramati, taṃ kāryaṃ na prāpayiṣyati; Vārāṇasyāṃ naimittikair (mss. nimi˚) dvādaśavarṣikānāvṛṣṭir vyākṛtā; rarely, pratyekabodhi is predicted, Vipaśyinā … sa sārthavāhaḥ pratyekabodhau vyākṛtaḥ; (sā Bhagavatā) pratyekāyāṃ bodhau vyākṛtā; much more commonly, in fact constantly in most texts, perfect enlightenment or Buddhahood is predicted, always by an earlier Buddha, who declares that the person mentioned will attain his goal, often in a particular age and world; this constitutes vyākaraṇa (3), and seems to come to be regarded as a regular, perhaps necessary, preliminary to Buddhahood in Mahāyāna; it always occurs long before the event, under a Buddha of the remote past, tho it may be the Buddha immediately preceding the one for whom the prediction is made; sometimes a group prediction is made, all to become Buddhas in turn and each one to predict the next, (vs) paraṃparā eva tathānyam-anyaṃ te vyākariṣyanti …; (vs) anyonya vyākarṣu (˚kārṣu?) tadāgrabodhaye; see also; the person predicted is always in the acc., or nom. in a passive expression; only seeming exceptions are (prose) saced asmākam api bhagavān, yatheme 'nye … vyākṛtā, evam asmākam api tathāgataḥ pṛthak-pṛthag vyākuryāt (in Buddhaʼs reply, line 9, ahaṃ … vaśībhūtaśatāny anantaraṃ vyākaromi), and (prose) yad bhagavān asmākaṃ vyākuryād … (asmākam is acc., as clearly elsewhere even in the prose of,); the goal is regularly loc., in prose commonly anuttarāyāṃ samyak-saṃbodhau [Page517-b] (abbreviated an˚ sam˚ in my citations); rarely what look like dat. forms occur, (above); (vs) yaṃ vyākṛtā sma paramāgrabodhaye; (vs) bodhisattvā ye vyākṛtā bodhayi (m.c. for ˚ye); (prose) anuttarāye samyaksaṃbodhaye, but below 17—18 vyākṛto … anuttarāye (v.l. ˚yāṃ!) samyaksaṃbodhāye (so both mss., em. ˚aye, but a loc. is surely intended); these rare -bodhaye forms may actually intend locs., see; rather often, no goal is expressed in words at all, so that the verb vyākaroti itself means predicts (someone) unto enlightenment (examples below); or the goal may be stated in a following direct quotation, as in (vs) te vyākriyante … bhaviṣyathā buddha …, they are prophesied, ‘you shall become Buddhas’; typical examples, (Śrīgarbhaṃ nāma) bodhisattvaṃ … an˚ sam˚ vyākṛtya; yadāpi (sc. māṃ) vyākurvasi agrabodhau (vs); … nāma bodhisattvaṃ … vyākṛtyān˚ sam˚; vayaṃ bhagavatā … an˚ sam˚ vyākṛtāḥ; tān vyākaromī aham … tathāgatatve (vs); catasraḥ parṣado vyākaromy an˚ sam˚, similarly 10; nāhaṃ … vyākṛtā cān˚ sam˚; (yāvad …) bodhisattvā na vyākṛtā bhaviṣyanti an˚ sam˚; ātmasamatāye (em.; loc.) samāsataḥ svayaṃbhūsamatāye vyākārṣīt; samanantara-vyākṛto … anuttarāyāṃ (so mss.) samyaksaṃbuddhāya (v.l. ˚yā, prob. loc.,);, see above; no goal expressed (besides some cited above), vyākṛto hy eṣa Śāriputro (vs); na tāvad asmān saṃbuddho vyākaroti (vs); vyākṛtā yada bheṣyāmas (vs); (yenāyaṃ bhagavān prathamata) evaṃ vyākṛtaḥ; no cāhaṃ (tehi) vyākṛto; , also spelled viyūha chiefly in vss, and cf. vyūhā; m., (1) (as in Skt. and Pali, mass, heap) mass, large amount: yā kāci rati-viyūhā divyā (vs) = Tib. lha yi dgaḥ ba rnam maṅ ji sñed pa, what large quantities of divine pleasures; (2) in Mahāyāna works (not in Pali), arrangement, but with regular overtones of marvelous, supernatural, magical arrangement, esp. of Buddhafields; Tib. bkod pa; orderly arrangement, but it is more than that; the related ḥgod pa is also rendered decorate, adorn, and vyūha implies {{magnificerice->magnificence||20210831||https://github.com/sanskrit-lexicon/csl-corrections/issues/80|}}, splendor, as well as supernatural qualities; it seems very close to Skt. vibhūti as used e.g. in ch. 10 (see note 3 on vs 7 of my transl.), and supernal manifestation, which I chose for vibhūti, would do for BHS vyūha; note (prose) tāṃś ca vyūhān vibhūtiṃ dṛṣṭvā bodhisattvasya, Māraḥ …, seeing the Bodhisattvaʼs supernal manifestations and marvelous power (splendor), Māra … The word is used in such titles as Sukhāvatī-vyūha, Gaṇḍa-vyūha, with this mg., and is a special favorite in and; the translations of,, and fumble it for the most part; hence the above attempt to make it clear; it seems to me essentially simple, tho no one English word is appropriate: (nāsmābhir eṣu … buddha-)kṣetravyūheṣu vā bodhisattvavikrīḍiteṣu vā … spṛhotpāditā, we conceived no desire for … these supernal manifestations (or arrangements) of the Buddha-fields …; kṣetreṣu buddhāna śruṇitva vyūhān (vs); Raśmiprabhāsasya viyūha bheṣyati (vs), the supernal manifestation of (the future Buddha) Raśmiprabhāsa shall exist (in his Buddha-field, just described; viyūha n. sg., not loc. with and); sarveṣa etādṛśakāś ca vyūhā … tatha buddhakṣetraṃ (vs), all (the Buddhas just mentioned) shall have just such supernal manifestations, and also (a) Buddha-field(s); (Ānanda, for whom Buddhahood has just been predicted) ātmanaś ca buddhakṣetraguṇa-vyūhāñ śrutvā, hearing the supernal manifestations of excellent qualities in his own (future) Buddha-field; sarvākāraguṇopetā (v.l. ˚to) buddhakṣetraguṇa-vyūhā (v.l. ˚ho) bhaviṣyanti (no v.l. recorded); samāś caiṣāṃ buddhakṣetraguṇavyūhā bhaviṣyanti; (tathāgatādhiṣṭhānena tathāgata-)balādhānena tathāgatavikrīḍitena tathāgatavyūhena (by the Tathāgataʼs supernal manifestation) tathāgatābhyudgatajñānena (all the parallel words mean substantially by the Tathāgataʼs supernatural power); bodhimaṇḍaparipālakair devaputrais tādṛśā vyūhā bodhimaṇḍa abhinirmitā (q.v.) abhūvan; tāṃś ca vyūhān dṛṣṭvā 7; ye ca kecin mahāvyūhāḥ (sc. buddha-)kṣetrakoṭīṣv anantakāḥ (vs); Chap. 20 of is entitled Bodhimaṇḍa-vyūha-parivartaḥ; in it the word is frequent, e.g. ratnachattra-vyūhaḥ, manifestation of a jewelled umbrella; prabhā-v˚, referring to the ekaratnajāla of, which prob. means single-jewel-magic, a magical manifestation of a brilliant jewel (or jewels); buddhakṣetraguṇa-vyūhās (as above), displayed at the bodhimaṇḍa; tebhyaḥ sarva-vyūhebhya iyaṃ gāthā niścarati sma; sarvaguṇa-vyūhaṃ kūṭāgāraṃ; kasyāyam evaṃrūpaḥ kūṭāgāra-vyūhaḥ; etc.; at beginning of next chapter, referring back to chapter 20, ima evaṃrūpā vyūhā … bodhimaṇḍe 'bhisaṃskṛtā abhūvan; dṛṣṭā sa viyūha śobhanā (ed. so˚) bodhimaṇḍasmi marūbhi (so m.c. for text maru˚) yā kṛtā (vs); (tataś ca) prabhāvyūhād imā gāthā niścaranti sma, and from this manifestation of splendor (of the Buddha) …; yā bodhimaṇḍi prakṛtā ca surair viyūhā, yā vā viyūha kṛta sarva(-?)jinātmajebhiḥ, sā sarva saṃsthita viyūha ti dharmacakre (at the dharmacakra-pravartana; [Page520-b] sā suggests that viyūha may be f., see vyūhā); buddhakṣetra-vyūha-; ahaṃ (sc. buddha-)kṣetravyūhān niṣpādayiṣyāmi; many others could be added; other cases of viyūha,.

, (1) nt., some kind of ornament: ˚kam, in a list of ornaments; Tib. mkhaḥ rten, see below; (2) m. and nt., = Tib. mkhaḥ rten, rendered by the firmament; sky supporting; a sort of ornament.
